findings.description: The assembled suite runs green with nothing dropped: 120 cases, exit 0, no skips, and every per-file @test floor met.
findings.evidence:
$ timeout 300 bats tests/  -> SUITE EXIT=0
1..120
ok lines: 120 / not ok lines: 0
grep -ci '# skip' over the TAP output -> 0 (exit 1, no skipped case)
$ /usr/bin/grep -c '^@test' tests/<file>:
  apps 18 (floor 18), doctor 11 (11), font 44 (44), install-failures 17 (17),
  jsonc 9 (9), licensed-fonts 7 (7), packages 13 (13) = 119 across the seven
  pre-existing files; tests/lint.bats adds 1, total 120.
$ git diff 61213fe..HEAD -- tests/ | /usr/bin/grep -qE '^\+[[:space:]]*skip\b' -> exit 1
  (exit 1 is the passing case; not exit 2, so the check did run)

findings.description: No bare [[ or (( survives anywhere on the guarded surface, including tests/install-failures.bats, which two tasks edited and no task owned.
findings.evidence:
$ /usr/bin/grep -nE '^[[:space:]]*(\[\[|\(\()' tests/*.bats tests/helpers.bash tests/mutation-check.sh
(no output)
B-1 exit=1  -- exit 1 with empty stdout is the pass; exit 2 (missing file / bad pattern)
would have been blocked, and did not occur. Run with /usr/bin/grep explicitly, not the
ugrep shim, per the constitution's note to checkers.
Confirmed in-suite as well: TAP line 'ok 107 no bare [[ or (( on the guarded surface'.

findings.description: Five commit messages, each covering why at least as much as what, each intelligible cold a year out; none merely restates its diff.
findings.evidence:
$ git log --format=%s 61213fe..HEAD (newest first):
  docs(memory): write down the bash 3.2 errexit rule and the incident behind it
  test: fail the suite if a bare [[ or (( comes back
  test: prove every converted assertion can still go red
  test: convert all 54 bare compound statements to forms that actually fail
  test: share the assertion helpers instead of hiding them in one file
Read in full from `git log --format=%B 61213fe..HEAD`. Each body argues a cause, not a filelist:
- 72154e3 opens on why the helpers had to move -- bash 3.2 'throws away a failing [[ ]] unless
  that construct is the enclosing function's literal last statement' -- and closes on drift:
  'one definition of each name rather than seven'.
- 6cc4fce reproduces the bug inline ('f() { [[ 1 -eq 2 ]]; echo reached; } prints reached and
  exits 0 under set -e') and then argues down #21's figure of 24 with the loop counterexample,
  which is why there is no safe-by-position carve-out. Records the two judgment calls
  (packages.bats:146, doctor.bats:244) with the reasoning for each.
- 7282d89 states why exit status is not the proof: 'a mutation that breaks bash parsing collapses
  the file to a synthetic not ok 1 setup_file failed with the mutated case never running at all',
  and volunteers the harness's own near-miss (a heredoc tracker blind to <<-'STUB' silently
  reported zero sites for font.bats).
- f317a69 explains why the guard is a bats case rather than a script ('a second entry point is one
  a contributor or a CI job can forget about'), why a first-token grep was not enough (a planted
  `true; [[ 1 -eq 2 ]]` passed it), and why if/while/until conditions are deliberately unscanned.
- 814d917 says why an unexplained convention fails ('the kind that gets overridden the first time
  it looks inconvenient') and carries the #17 incident behind the rule.
None is a restatement of its diff; all five would read cold.

  814d917 remote-branches: []
  f317a69 remote-branches: []

findings.description: The worker's index-only split claim holds: the committed tree over tests/ is byte-identical to the working tree, so what the suite verifies is what got committed.
findings.evidence:
$ git diff 61213fe..HEAD -- tests/  > range.diff   (974 lines)
$ git diff 61213fe      -- tests/  > wt.diff
$ diff range.diff wt.diff -> exit 0, no output.
The commit-range diff and the baseline-to-working-tree diff are the same 974 lines, so HEAD's
tests/ tree equals the tree the 120-case green run above was taken against.
